find: Ohm's Law states that \(V = I \times R\) where V is potential difference in volts, I is current in amperes, and R is resistance in ohms (Ω). This relationship only applies to ohmic conductors at constant temperature.
replace: \(V = I \times R\), where V is potential difference in volts, I is current in amperes, and R is resistance in ohms (Ω). You can use this equation for any component. Ohm's law is the separate rule that an ohmic conductor at constant temperature keeps a constant resistance, so its current is directly proportional to the potential difference across it.
note: F5: V = IR applies to every component; only the proportionality is limited to ohmic conductors.
